claude.performance_metric: 2011 sales $2.8bn (+28.4%); returned to net income $368.2m after 2010 net loss $214.2m driven by $400.4m EC Fine indemnification; no divestiture
claude.rationale: The slice documents an integrated engineering/manufacturing organization (~1,557 R&D employees) operating at global scale with growing sales and no reported product/operations incoherence, so p4 = 0. It also reports no operations-vs-organization fracture — no restructuring, culture clash, or management breakdown against operations is documented; the business ran as a going concern with no divestiture or break-up, so p5 = 0. The one documented cross-boundary disruption is a legacy EC Fine indemnification liability absorbed via a contractual agreement, which is a financial/legal drag, not a product/process or process/organization interface failure. Controlling-intent archetype is uncertain because the slice deliberately excludes deal-structure framing.

gemini.performance_metric: Sales for 2011 were $2.8 billion, an increase of 28.4%
gemini.rationale: The slice documents WABCO operating as a going concern with an integrated engineering and manufacturing organization. There is no evidence of product/process disruption (p4) or process/organization fracture (p5) during the outcome window.

grok.rationale: The slice documents no product/process interface disruption: the registrant maintained an integrated engineering and manufacturing organization (~1,557 employees on new products/processes) and grew sales 28.4% to $2.8 billion with no reported product-line/operations incoherence. No process/organization fracture is documented either; the firm continued as a stand-alone going concern with no break-up of the core business, the only material negative being a $400.4 million legacy EC Fine indemnification charge from the former parent's Bath and Kitchen business, not an operations-vs-organization integration failure.
